messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] INLA clinear summary question
parts:
On Fri, 2015-05-08 at 08:47 -0700, SJB wrote:
> Dear INLA community,
>
> I am using the INLA latent model clinear among other linear effects
> (paramaterised in the usual way)
>
> e.g f(V, model='clinear',range=c(0,Inf),initial=1)
>
> Once the model is fit I can get the coefficient on my clinear variable
> by either using summary(model) or model$summary.hyperpar.
>
> My question is how would i recreate this value from the values
> returned from model$summary.random$V?
>
> model$summary.random$V returns multiple columns, and my understanding
> is the ID column are the unique values and the rest are summaries of
> the effect size (mean,sd etc).
>
> However I dont seem to be able to get the same clinear coefficient
> from manipulating model$summary.random$V that compares with
> summary(model) or model$summary.hyperpar.


Hi,

the output of summary.random$... is the summary of 'beta*x', where the
'x' is the ones are defined in '$ID'.

you can see this more clearly, doing the example in inla.doc("clinear")



> r=inla(y ~ f(x, model = "clinear", range = c(1,
Inf)),data=data.frame(y,x),control.inla = list(int.strategy="eb"))
